guide.title: How to get a GitHub token

intro.title: What is a GitHub token?
intro.body: A GitHub personal access token is a secure way to authenticate yourself so apps can access the GitHub API on your behalf.

step1.title: Step 1: Visit the GitHub token settings page
step1.description: Click the link below to open the settings page.

step2.title: Step 2: Generate a new token
items: Click "Generate new token" on the settings page.

step3.title: Step 3: Set the token name and permissions

items.name: Enter a descriptive name, such as "GitHub Star Manager".
items.expiration: Choose an expiration time (30 days or longer is recommended).

list: public_repo - access public repositories
read:user - read user information (optional)

step4.title: Step 4: Generate and copy the token
items: Scroll to the bottom and click "Generate token".
Important: copy the generated token immediately (e.g. ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx).
The token is shown only once; regenerate it if you lose it.

step5.title: Step 5: Save the token in this app
step5.description: Paste the token into the input above and click Save.

security.title: Security tips
items: Treat the token like a password - do not share it.
Revoke the token on GitHub immediately if it leaks.
Tokens are stored locally and never uploaded.

delete.note: Set a new token if you want to keep syncing data.

help.title: API usage guide
steps: 1) Create API: click Add API, then fill in name, type, and credentials.
2) Assign modules: choose a compatible API in each module dropdown; incompatible options are hidden automatically.
3) Enable modules: after choosing an API, toggle the switch to enable the module.
4) Deletion warning: removing an API in use will disable the related modules.
